# Uniform properness and an exact linear bound on total buffered force

The vanishing-buffer theorem has two quantitative consequences. All deepest
sources have a uniform atomic gap, and every nonvertical through-source
buffered plane cuts a fixed own inball properly. In a SAME-separator finite
contact dual this bounds the total response coefficient K=sum kappa.

The actual logarithmic volume rows then give the exact entropy identity

    log(epsilon K/Delta)
       =KL(sigma||w)+[K_V+sum_a sigma_a log(M/E_a)]/(d+1),

where w_a=kappa_a/K, sigma_a=kappa_a delta_a/Delta, and
delta_a=epsilon(L_a E_a/M)^(1/(d+1)). In particular Delta<=epsilon K,
which improves mere o(1) to O(epsilon) without bounding the individual L_a.
This is a response-scaling theorem, not a Gamma payment.

## 1. Geometric hypotheses and uniform constants

Use the global joint bad-minimum (or o(1)-optimal-value) setting of
`candidate cebc39c4f5ccbc96`.
The canonical cardinality-minimal bad-base compactness/quota framework is an
explicit hypothesis. It supplies fixed finite P, positive limiting fibers,
bounded continuous geometry, and positive definite within-fiber covariance.
Write N=d+1 and suppress the sequence index. Choose constants such that

    |K_z|>=v>0,     K_z subset R Ball_d,
    lambda_- I <=Sigma<=lambda_+ I,   lambda_->0.

The preceding theorem gives

    delta_max=max_(z,X in K_z)
                   epsilon [L(z,X)E_(K_z)(X)/M]^(1/N) ->0.     (1)

All actual deepest marks also have a common own inball radius r>0, by the
proved positive-depth lower bound, boundary support planes, and vanishing
physical buffers. These statements require no regular cap menu or source
martingale. Denote the actual maximum raw buffered depth by Q.

Set omega_(d-1)=volume of the unit (d-1)-ball, with omega_0=1. The total
Euclidean unit-normal section-area bound and its covariance-normalized form are

    A=|P| omega_(d-1) R^(d-1),
    S_max=A sqrt(lambda_+).                            (2)

The slab comparison holds with these constants for arbitrary base tilts and
all supporting statuses.

## 2. Every deepest base has a uniform strict atomic gap

For an arbitrary mark Y=(p,y), increasing its thresholds by the buffer adds
at most S_max delta_max of mass to every nonvertical cap. Pure-base cap masses
do not change. Therefore

    D_0(Y)<=D_epsilon(Y)<=D_0(Y)+S_max delta_max.        (3)

The exact ordinary bound proved in the preceding note is

    D_0(p,y)<=baseDepth(p)-|K_p|/2.

At a deepest mark this gives

    baseDepth(p)-Q >= |K_p|/2-S_max delta_max.

For all sufficiently small epsilon, (1) makes the right side at least v/4:

    baseDepth(p)-Q >= v/4 >0                          (4)

for EVERY deepest base. Thus there are no atomic deepest groups in this small
epsilon regime. This is uniform and does not merely say that each individual
finite-epsilon source has some possibly vanishing base gap. In rank zero use
the formal baseDepth=M; there are no actual nonzero pure-base directions.

## 3. Uniform own coareas for every buffered through-source normal

Normalize a nonzero continuous normal by Gamma(u)=sqrt(u^T Sigma u)=1.
Then

    1/sqrt(lambda_+) <= ||u|| <= 1/sqrt(lambda_-).

At a deepest Y=(p,y), every buffered through-source cut has own-fiber plane

    u.(X-y)=-delta_Y.

Its distance from y is at most delta_max sqrt(lambda_+). Once this is <r/2,
the plane crosses the actual ball B(y,r) in a (d-1)-ball of radius at least
sqrt(3)r/2. Thus EVERY such own trace is proper, not just a selected minimizing
direction, and its coarea is bounded below by

    S_min=omega_(d-1)(sqrt(3)r/2)^(d-1) sqrt(lambda_-)>0. (5)

Its coarea is the section area divided by ||u||. Every total effective coarea
T_j used by an actual supporting-response branch therefore satisfies

    S_min<=T_j<=S_max.                                (6)

The upper bound allows every sampled fiber to contribute its maximal section;
inside or outside facet selectors in [0,1] can only decrease that bound. The
own contribution in (5) is proper and hence has no selector ambiguity. Formula
(6) retains nonsmooth supporting contacts at OTHER fibers. For d=1 the same
statement uses the actual interior point section of H_0 measure one.

## 4. Exact finite-contact dual normalization

This part is conditional on the SAME joint physical/parameter separator from
the audited conservative nonregular finite-contact construction in
`candidate 1a7cfa3d1047cbae`.
All of its actual-response hypotheses remain in force. The geometric results
above do not by themselves assert a separator or a differentiable optimized
parameter. In particular no unrelated parameter-only certificate may be
substituted in the following identities.

Index the covering groups by i, their actual finite contact marks by a, and
effective outside branches/selectors by b. Let rho_ij>=0 sum to one over the
caps of group i. Its harmonic coefficient is

    B_ib=sum_j rho_ij/T_ijb.

By (6),

    1/S_max<=B_ib<=1/S_min.                            (7)

Write lambda_iab>=0 for the common separator weights. Because all deepest
groups are proper by (4), their total is one and no atomic row remains. Define

    kappa_ia=sum_b lambda_iab/B_ib,
    K=sum_(i,a) kappa_ia.

Then (7) yields the exact uniform bounds

    S_min<=K<=S_max.                                  (8)

Repeated occurrences of the same actual mark can be merged by adding their
kappa. Keep the notation a for either these merged marks or their original
finite occurrences; both conventions give the same sums. Put

    E_a=E_(K_(p_a))(y_a),  L_a=L(Y_a),
    delta_a=epsilon (L_a E_a/M)^(1/N)>0,
    Delta=sum_a kappa_a delta_a>0,
    w_a=kappa_a/K,
    sigma_a=kappa_a delta_a/Delta.                     (9)

Discard zero kappa; then w and sigma are positive probabilities on the SAME
finite index set. Shared cap-normal controls and multiple contacts are already
encoded in the audited kappa_ia; no singleton per-cap centroid assertion is
made here. What is required is that the parameter component of this SAME
separator supplies the exact volume contact rows with the sigma in (9).

## 5. The same-separator volume entropy identity

Let rho_a be those probability rows. Their exact identities are

    E_(rho_a) w=Y_a,       E_(rho_a)L=L_a,
    sum_a (sigma_a/L_a)rho_a=dm/(M L),
    (1/M) integral log L dm=0.

Define the original-volume probability rows d bar_rho_a=(L/L_a)d rho_a.
Then sum_a sigma_a bar_rho_a=dm/M. Their relative entropy is finite at every
positive finite-parameter pair and gives the exact nonnegative quantity

    K_V:=sum_a sigma_a KL(bar_rho_a||rho_a)
        =-sum_a sigma_a log L_a >=0.                  (10)

Indeed log(d bar_rho_a/d rho_a)=log L-log L_a. Summing against the actual
original-volume row mixture cancels the first term by logarithmic
normalization. This uses the volume coupling only, not a surface coupling.

From (9),

    sum_a sigma_a log delta_a
       =log epsilon-[K_V+sum_a sigma_a log(M/E_a)]/N.   (11)

Each E_a is positive and at most |K_(p_a)|<=M, because the projective energy
is a minimum that can be tested at parameter zero. Thus every additional
log(M/E_a) is nonnegative; no estimated constant is needed here.

On the other hand sigma_a/w_a=delta_a/(Delta/K). Hence the finite discrete
relative entropy satisfies

    KL(sigma||w)
       =sum_a sigma_a log delta_a-log(Delta/K).         (12)

Combining (11) and (12) proves the EXACT identity

    log(epsilon K/Delta)
       = KL(sigma||w)
          +[K_V+sum_a sigma_a log(M/E_a)]/N >=0.        (13)

Equivalently Jensen's inequality for x log x under w gives
log(Delta/K)<=sum sigma log delta, and (11) supplies its upper bound.
The exact entropy form retains the deficit rather than discarding it.

In particular

    0<Delta<=epsilon K<=epsilon S_max.                 (14)

This conclusion is valid at each sufficiently small-epsilon pair satisfying
the stated same-separator hypotheses; it is not merely a subsequential limit.
There is no implied lower bound comparable to epsilon and no pointwise bound
delta_a<=epsilon or L_a<=1.

## 6. Additional scaled-entropy bounds and retained scope

Writing I=log(epsilon K/Delta)>=0, equation (13) gives
Delta=epsilon K exp(-I). Since I exp(-I)<=1/e,

    Delta I<=epsilon K/e,
    Delta KL(sigma||w)<=epsilon S_max/e,
    Delta K_V<=N epsilon S_max/e.                     (15)

These control the appropriately weighted VOLUME entropies even if their
unscaled values diverge. They do not identify or bound an independent surface
logarithmic reserve. In particular Delta=O(epsilon) alone does not justify
discarding a pointwise surface term Delta log L when log L has no uniform
boundary bound.

The geometric conclusions (4)--(6) remove atomic deepest rows and own-support
degeneracy in the stated joint limiting setting. They do not remove inside or
outside supporting facets at other fibers, give a rate of convergence of L,
or solve the remaining physical cap-payment inequality. The normalization in
(9) and the SAME separator in (10) are essential; choosing independent volume
and physical dual weights would invalidate (13).

## 7. An actual sharp calibration

For n=0,d=1 take the interval [-1,1], L=1, and its centroid source y=0.
Here M=E=2, Sigma=1/3 and delta=epsilon. For 0<epsilon<1 the two
Gamma-normalized cap normals are u=+sqrt(3),-sqrt(3), and both caps are proper.
Their coareas are 1/sqrt(3). The balanced group has rho_+=rho_-=1/2, hence

    B=sqrt(3),   kappa=K=1/sqrt(3),
    sigma=w=1,  K_V=0,  log(M/E)=0,
    Delta=epsilon/sqrt(3)=epsilon K.

This is an actual fixed-body global parameter optimum: every positive concave
log-normalized U has U(0)>=1 by Jensen, so its source buffer cannot improve
on L=1. The L=1 maximum is uniquely at zero, since its raw depth at y is
1-|y|+(epsilon/sqrt(3))sqrt(1-y^2), with the smaller cap never saturated for
0<epsilon<1. All intervals are affinely equivalent in the invariant buffer
normalization, so this is also a joint interval/body optimum in this safe
one-fiber class. It is not an OC-bad example. It shows that the coefficient
one in Delta<=epsilon K cannot be improved without additional information.

The companion `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_total_buffer_force_identity_defect_transport.py` passes
245 exact checks. Its arbitrary rational finite arrays check the algebra only
and are explicitly not asserted to be geometric contact rows; the single-
interval equality calibration above is actual.
